claims.text: A tailored post-casting heat treatment can induce coherent nanoscale precipitates at internal lamellar boundaries in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Inducing these precipitates will improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the as-cast lamellar microstructure.
The initial eutectic HEA contains fine dual-phase lamellar colonies, such as FCC/B2 colonies.
The initial lamellar colonies have continuous, brittle interphase boundaries.
Microcracks tend to nucleate at these interphase boundaries under tensile loading and cause premature failure.
Controlling heat-treatment temperature, time, and cooling rate can make nanoprecipitates nucleate preferentially along lamellar boundaries without coarsening.
Coherent nanoprecipitates provide obstacles to dislocation motion and thereby improve yield strength.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that can cause premature crack initiation.
Decorating lamellar boundaries with coherent precipitates will reduce stress concentration specifically at the original continuous brittle boundaries.
Reduced boundary stress concentration will mitigate microcrack initiation and enhance tensile ductility.
The intervention is applicable to eutectic HEAs with fine lamellar dual-phase microstructures under room-temperature tensile conditions.
Precipitate coarsening can prevent the anticipated strength and ductility improvements.
Loss of phase stability can prevent the anticipated strength and ductility improvements.
The exact strength and ductility improvements depend on the detailed microstructural evolution.
The expected coherent precipitate evolution remains to be fully characterized in eutectic HEAs.
